returned_textual_content: # Model roles and permissions Not every user is equal when we’re talking about using Solidatus models. A model owner is in complete control over which users and/or [groups](/models/share-and-collaborate/groups) have access to the model, and what actions they can perform, via four unique model roles: Owner, Author, Approver, and Viewer. {% hint style="success" %} The same general points apply to managing access to [Data Domains](/data-domains/build-data-domains/edit-data-domains#data-domain-roles-and-permissions), [Agents](/connectors/connectors-overview/users-and-tokens#agent-roles), and [Jobs](/connectors/connectors-overview/users-and-tokens#job-roles), but the role types and their permissions in these contexts are different. Please view the pages for each feature for specific role types and permissions. {% endhint %} ## Share a model and assign roles There are a number of ways to share a model with other registered Solidatus users or groups and to set their model roles: * Within the [Model Overview](/the-user-interface/models-ui/model-overview#permissions), use the *Permissions* section of the *Settings* tab. * Within the [Model Overview](/the-user-interface/models-ui/model-overview#summary-tab), use the `PEOPLE` section on the `Summary` page. * Within the [Model Overview](/the-user-interface/models-ui/model-overview#actions-menu), click the `ACTIONS` button in the top right and select `Manage Sharing`. ## Permissions for each model role Each role permits a unique set of actions to be performed relative to a given model. The following table lists the permissions available for each model role. {% hint style="warning" %} Remember that a user registered with a Consumer (read-only) or Practitioner licence **will not** be able to perform many actions permitted by Owner, Author, Approver, or Viewer roles, even if they are assigned these roles on a model. {% endhint %} | **Action** | **Owner** | **Author** | **Approver** | **Viewer** | | --------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------------ | ---------- | | Edit model settings and permissions | X | | | | | Delete the model | X | | | | | Merge Pull Request / task / model import update | X | X | | | | Create, edit, and assign tasks | X | X | | | | Edit the model directly (without creating a Fork) | X | X | | | | Approve activities | X | X | X | | | View model and model history | X | X | X | X | | View tasks/Pull Requests/model import updates | X | X | X | X | | Comment on tasks/Pull Requests/model import updates | X | X | X | X | | Create and edit a model Fork | X | X | X | X | | Submit Pull Request from Fork | X | X | X | X | | Export the model | X | X | X | X | {% hint style="warning" %} Dashboards, Agents, and Jobs have their own specific roles - see [Data Domain Roles](/data-domains/build-data-domains/edit-data-domains#data-domain-roles-and-permissions), [Agent Roles](/connectors/connectors-overview/users-and-tokens#agent-roles), and [Job Roles](/connectors/connectors-overview/users-and-tokens#job-roles). {% endhint %} ## Useful facts about model roles * The user that creates a model is automatically assigned the Owner role on that model, and, therefore, can share the model with other users or groups. * More than one user or group is allowed to own a model, and any Owner can assign and remove other owners (as long as at least one owner remains). * An individual user may have been assigned a role for a model directly and/or inherited a role via their membership of one or more groups. * When checking what role a user has on a model, Solidatus will take the union of all the capabilities provided to them, whether assigned directly to that user or to one or more groups that the user is a member of. The Model Overview provides a checkbox called `Show inherited roles` so you can see all roles each user has on the model. In the example below a model has a single owner, and a group has been given permission to view the model - but who is in that group? Click `Show inherited roles` and the single entry for the group is replaced by a list of the users in the group. Note that the model Owner (Demo User2) is a member of the group - they acquire the Viewer role via the group, but their role as Owner is more powerful.
